title: SLAI T-Rex: Post-training a Trillion-Param MoE on Ascend Chips
hook: Full-parameter post-training of the DeepSeek-V4 family on Huawei's Ascend NPUs — not NVIDIA GPUs — hitting a 2.93x efficiency jump over the open-source baseline.
key_points: Targets full-parameter post-training of trillion-parameter MoE models on the Ascend NPU SuperPOD, an alternative to GPU clusters.
Hierarchical optimization across three layers: model parallelism, computation–communication orchestration, and low-level kernel execution.
Reaches 34.22% Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) — a 2.93x improvement over the open-source baseline recipe — while staying training-stable.
Adds a CPT + SFT pipeline for Operations Research, using solver-verified synthetic optimization documents (10K samples).
The specialized DeepSeek-V4-Flash tops the evaluated models at 71.81% zero-shot Pass@1, beating GPT-5.4-Mini by 3.98 points.
content_html: Full-parameter post-training of trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts models is brutal on a training system: severe memory pressure, communication that won't overlap with compute, and inefficient kernels. Dongfang Li, Xiaodong Luo, Ruoyu Sun, and a large team report doing it not on GPUs but on Huawei's Ascend NPU SuperPOD, using the DeepSeek-V4 family as the workload — and packaging the result as a framework they call SLAI T-Rex.
extra_html:
How it works

The authors build a hierarchical optimization framework spanning three levels: model-level parallelism, computation–communication orchestration (overlapping the two so the network doesn't stall the math), and low-level kernel execution. On the Ascend NPU SuperPOD this reaches 34.22% Model FLOPs Utilization — a 2.93x improvement over the open-source baseline recipe — while maintaining training stability.

Why it matters

Almost all large-scale LLM training is built around GPU clusters, so an end-to-end recipe that hits competitive utilization on non-NVIDIA hardware is a meaningful data point on hardware diversity. On top of the infrastructure, the team builds a continued-pretraining and supervised-fine-tuning pipeline for Operations Research tasks, using solver-verified synthetic optimization documents (10K SFT samples across four task categories). The resulting DeepSeek-V4-Flash specialization reports the highest average zero-shot Pass@1 among the models evaluated, 71.81%, outperforming GPT-5.4-Mini by 3.98 points and the base Flash model by 11.27. See the arXiv report for the full system details.

related.title: DeepSeek-V4: Sparse Attention, Million-Token Default
related.hook: DeepSeek-V4 makes a 1M-token context window the default and pairs token-wise compression with sparse attention, so long-context inference no longer pays the usual compute and memory tax.

related.title: Megatron-LM: Training LLMs with Model Parallelism
related.hook: Split the big matrices inside attention and MLP layers across GPUs, add a few communication ops, and you can train an 8.3B model on 512 GPUs — no custom compiler needed.

related.title: The Hardware Lottery
related.hook: A research idea can win not because it is genuinely better, but because it happens to fit the hardware and software we already have. Sara Hooker calls this the hardware lottery.
